title: ProvAttribution
description: Rootless facet — PROV Attribution: "the ascribing of an entity to an agent". When an entity is attributed to an agent, the entity was generated by some unspecified activity that in turn was associated to the agent; the relation is useful when the activity is not known, or irrelevant. Composed onto a statement, the statement is the attributed entity. PROV mandates only an identifiable agent; the agent identification scheme is not prescribed. Source: W3C PROV-DM (REC-prov-dm-20130430) §5.3.2 Attribution, wasAttributedTo(id; e, ag, attrs); PROV-O prov:wasAttributedTo.

id.description: Optional identifier for this attribution relation (PROV-DM §5.7.1: two attributions are equal if they have the same identifier).

agent.description: The agent whom the entity is ascribed to, and therefore bears some responsibility for its existence (PROV-DM §5.3.2, ag, mandatory). Must be identifiable (§5.7.1); the identification scheme is unprescribed by PROV.

attributes.description: Optional set of attribute-value pairs with additional information about this attribution (PROV-DM attrs; reserved PROV attributes per §5.7.2 — prov:label, prov:type — plus application-specific attributes, PROV-DM's extensibility point, §6).
